disclosures.text: A suction chuck for non-contact holding of a thin, flat workpiece by suction
A flat main body with a compressed gas flow path formed inside
A facing surface on the main body facing the workpiece
Multiple recesses formed on the facing surface as suction elements
The recesses generate negative pressure by ejecting compressed gas
The facing surface is similar in shape to the workpiece or offset outward from the workpiece shape
The facing surface completely encloses the workpiece shape when viewed perpendicularly
All recesses are arranged to be enclosed within the workpiece shape when viewed perpendicularly

A suction chuck for non-contact holding of a thin, flat workpiece, comprising a flat main body with an internal compressed gas flow path, and a facing surface on the main body facing the workpiece, the facing surface having multiple recesse
The facing surface and workpiece shape are right-angled quadrilaterals when viewed perpendicularly
Exhaust holes are opened in the facing surface around the recesses
The exhaust holes discharge compressed gas ejected from the recesses
All exhaust holes are arranged to be enclosed within the workpiece shape when viewed perpendicularly
Multiple recesses are aligned parallel to the sides of the facing surface when viewed perpendicularly
The recesses are cylindrical
The main body includes ejection flow paths for ejecting compressed gas along the inner wall of the recesses
The ejection flow paths are formed parallel to the facing surface
Multiple ejection flow paths are formed for one recess
The main body is formed by joining multiple plates in the thickness direction
The plates include a first plate with the facing surface and a second plate connected to a compressed gas source
The first plate has opening holes forming at least part of the recesses, opening to the facing surface
The ejection flow paths are located between the facing surface and the second plate
The second plate has a connection port for the compressed gas source on the side opposite the first plate
The second plate has supply grooves on the first plate-facing side, forming supply flow paths to guide compressed gas to the ejection flow paths
An intermediate plate is placed between the first and second plates
The intermediate plate has slits forming the ejection flow paths, penetrating in the thickness direction
A third plate is placed between the first and second plates
The third plate has connection holes to connect the ejection flow paths and the supply grooves
One side of the third plate in the thickness direction forms part of the inner wall of the ejection flow path
The other side of the third plate in the thickness direction closes the open side of the supply groove, forming the supply flow path
At least one supply flow path is connected to multiple ejection flow paths
Multiple supply flow paths are provided
Combinations of connection ports and ejection flow paths connected by each supply flow path are independent
All multiple plates are made of metal
The main body is formed by diffusion bonding all stacked plates
The multiple plates are made of stainless steel, aluminum alloy, or titanium alloy
All multiple plates are made of the same metal material
At least one of the recesses or ejection flow paths is formed by etching
At least one of the recesses or ejection flow paths is formed by machining
At least one of the connection ports or supply grooves is formed by machining
A workpiece transfer device comprising the suction chuck and a compressed gas source
The amount of compressed gas ejected from recesses at the center of the facing surface is greater than from recesses at the ends
The device separates the top workpiece from a stacked bundle and holds it with the suction chuck
Compressed gas is supplied to recesses at the ends of the facing surface first
Compressed gas is then supplied to recesses at the center of the facing surface to hold the top workpiece
A blowing device is provided to blow compressed gas towards the side of the workpiece bundle
A parallel mechanism is provided to move the workpiece held by the suction chuck
A SCARA arm is provided to move the workpiece held by the suction chuck
The workpiece is a solar cell wafer, fuel cell, secondary battery electrode, or separator
The suction chuck is lightweight
The suction chuck prevents workpiece damage from contact with edges during suction and release
The suction chuck is compact
The suction chuck is suitable for cleanroom environments with reduced flow rates
The recesses are arranged at equal intervals in vertical and horizontal directions
The exhaust holes are located between adjacent recesses in the vertical direction
The ejection flow paths are connected tangentially to the inner wall of the recesses
The ejection flow paths for adjacent recesses create swirling flows in opposite directions
The number of clockwise and counter-clockwise swirling flows is equal
The supply flow paths are divided into 2x4 regions on the facing surface
Each supply flow path connects one connection port and eight recesses
Compressed air is supplied to connection ports at one end of the facing surface first
Compressed air is then supplied to connection ports at the center of the facing surface
The timing of compressed air supply to each connection port is controlled by electromagnetic valves
The workpiece is peeled up from the end during suction
Compressed air is supplied sequentially from one corner to the other three corners of the facing surface
Guide members are fixed to the edge of the main body to regulate workpiece movement
The guide members are arranged in pairs opposite each other on each side of the main body
The guide members protrude below the facing surface
The blowing device has a cylindrical body with multiple blow-out holes
The blow-out holes are arranged in a line at equal intervals along the axis of the cylindrical body
The cylindrical body of the blowing device is rotatable about its axis
The blowing device blows air to the side of the workpiece bundle before or after suction starts at the corresponding end
The suction chuck reduces workpiece deformation compared to prior art
The suction chuck reduces workpiece vibration compared to prior art
The suction chuck is applicable to SCARA arm transfer robots
The suction chuck allows random access to workpieces in a stacked cassette
